title: Adaptive Shadow Benchmarking and Baseline Drift Detection in CI
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our current CI gating for performance focuses on single-point throughput snapshots (tokens/sec and p95) taken from one-off baseline runs. This produces noisy signals, misses slow baseline drift, and blocks PRs due to sporadic infra noise. Goal: Implement an adaptive shadow benchmarking pipeline that runs lightweight, representative perf workloads on PRs (shadow runs) and compares results against an autonomously maintained rolling baseline. The system should detect sustained regressions (drift) as well as single-PR regressions, minimize false positives, and be inexpensive enough to run frequently.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Shadow runs execute on every PR to selected affected models within budget (sampled fraction or low-cost configs). 2) The CI system computes tokens/sec and p95 with a rolling baseline per-model and per-sequence-length bucket. 3) Regressions are flagged when CUSUM or non-parametric tests indicate >3% degradation with p < 0.01 and reproduced across 2 independent runs. 4) PRs that fail perf gating get clear diagnostics: diff in throughput/p95, confidence interval, raw traces, and link to replay artifact. 5) Baseline update policy automatically incorporates stable new data and allows manual override. 6) False-positive rate < 2% on historical backtest (last 6 months).
implementation_notes: Architecture sketch: 1) PR Shadow Runner: lightweight distributed harness that replays a sampled micro-workload on dedicated low-priority infra; warms KV cache for realistic latency. 2) Baseline Service: per-model time-series store (daily buckets) with metadata (model version, quantization profile, seq-length distribution). 3) Drift Detector: dual-layer detection using Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) for gradual drift and Mann-Whitney U for per-PR delta significance. 4) Repro Engine: when a PR flags, schedule two reproducibility runs on isolated hardware. 5) CI Integration: gate policy in GitHub Actions/Linear PR check that marks PRs as Pass/Fail and attaches diagnostics. Key design choices: - Use stratified baselines by seq-length and batch size to reduce variance. - Cache-warm traces to avoid cold-start noise; measure cold vs warm separately. - Store raw token-level latency histograms in S3 for deep-dive analysis. - Cost control: run full synthetic suite only on merges; PRs get micro-sample (10% synthetic load + short replay).
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for detector logic with synthetic time-series (simulate gradual drift, step regressions, and noise). 2) Backtest on historical CI perf dataset (last 6 months) to validate thresholds and false-positive rate. 3) Canary: enable shadow runs for a small set of non-critical repos/models and compare to offline benchmarks. 4) Repro reliability tests: ensure 2-run repro reliably surfaces true regressions. 5) Load test the Baseline Service for 1000 per-day updates. 6) Create a flaky-run repository to exercise gating heuristics and ensure noise tolerance.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (week 1): deploy PR Shadow Runner and Baseline Service for internal model-dev team only; collect metrics. Stage 2 (week 2): expand to all model-serving repos and enable non-blocking perf checks in PRs. Stage 3 (week 3-4): flip gating to blocking for P0 changes and enable auto-repro for flagged PRs. Stage 4 (post rollout): monitor false-positive rate and tune detection thresholds; add dashboard panels and alerting for baseline drift. Emergency rollback: revert gating to non-blocking and disable shadow runs for impacted repos.
